proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(m=|\mathcal X|\) and
\[
 e_{p,n}=\left\{\frac{\log(6m/\alpha)}{2n}\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
We first establish the two probability bounds uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\).  Let \(Z\) be any random variable supported on \([0,1]\), and define \(\psi(\lambda)=\log E[\exp\{\lambda(Z-EZ)\}]\).  Under exponential tilting by \(\lambda\), differentiation under the expectation is valid because \(Z\) is bounded, and
\[
 \psi''(\lambda)=\operatorname{Var}_{\lambda}(Z)
 \le E_{\lambda}[(Z-1/2)^2]\le\frac14.
\]
Since \(\psi(0)=\psi'(0)=0\), two integrations give
\[
 \log E[\exp\{\lambda(Z-EZ)\}]\le\frac{\lambda^2}{8},
 \qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R.                                      \tag{1}
\]
For fixed \(x\in\mathcal X\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid}\) makes \(\widehat p_x\) the average of \(n\) independent Bernoulli random variables with common mean \(p_x\).  Applying exponential Markov inequality to their centered sum, using (1), and minimizing the exponent at \(\lambda=4e_{p,n}\), yields
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \bigl(|\widehat p_x-p_x|>e_{p,n}\bigr)
 \le 2\exp(-2ne_{p,n}^2)=\frac{\alpha}{3m}.                       \tag{2}
\]
The union bound over the finite set \(\mathcal X\) therefore gives
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \left(\max_{x\in\mathcal X}|\widehat p_x-p_x|\le e_{p,n}\right)
 \ge1-\frac\alpha3.                                                \tag{3}
\]
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), the vector \((p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\) is nonnegative and sums to one.  Hence \(\mathrm{def{:}mass\text{-}confidence\text{-}region}\) shows that the event in (3) is precisely \(\{(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\}\), and its coordinate bound is the asserted one.  Since the right-hand side of (2) is free of \(P\), the coverage in (3) is uniform over \(\mathcal M\).

For the count bound, let \(N\) be binomial with parameters \(n\) and \(p\).  For every \(t>0\), exponential Markov inequality and \(1-p+pe^{-t}\le\exp\{p(e^{-t}-1)\}\) imply
\[
 \Pr(N\le np/2)
 \le \exp\{tnp/2+np(e^{-t}-1)\}.
\]
At \(t=\log2\), the exponent is \(-np(1-\log2)/2\le-np/8\); the final inequality follows from \(\log2<3/4\), which in turn follows from \(e^{3/4}\ge1+3/4+(3/4)^2/2>2\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid}\) makes \(n_x\) binomial with parameters \(n\) and \(p_x\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) gives \(p_x\ge p_{\min}\), so another union bound gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \left(\min_{x\in\mathcal X}n_x<np_{\min}/2\right)
 &\le \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(n_x<np_x/2)\\
 &\le m\exp(-np_{\min}/8).                                      \tag{4}
 \end{aligned}
\]

It remains to bound mass profiling.  Let \(p=(p_x)\) and \(p'=(p'_x)\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), and fix \(f_x\in\mathscr F_n\) and \(q_x\in\mathscr Q_n(f_x)\) for each \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Define \(e_n=a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}\).  The continuum constraints in \(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\) imply, for every \(a\in I\),
\[
 f_x(a)\ge\kappa/2>0,
 \qquad |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)+e_n.
\]
Division is therefore valid.  Using the definition \(b_{\mu,n}=4e_n/\kappa\) from \(\mathrm{def{:}ecf\text{-}radii}\), we obtain
\[
 \left|\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|
 \le B_Y+\frac{2e_n}{\kappa}
 =B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2.                                         \tag{5}
\]
Both \(p\) and \(p'\) are within \(e_{p,n}\) of \(\widehat p\) in every coordinate by \(\mathrm{def{:}mass\text{-}confidence\text{-}region}\).  Thus \(|p_x-p'_x|\le2e_{p,n}\), and (5) plus the triangle inequality yields
\[
 \sup_{a\in I}\left|
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}(p_x-p'_x)\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}
 \right|
 \le2m\left(B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2\right)e_{p,n}.                 \tag{6}
\]

Finally, under the enlarged smoothness range in the core, put \(\gamma=\beta-1/2>0\).  The definitions in \(\mathrm{def{:}upper\text{-}tuning\text{-}grid}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}ecf\text{-}radii}\) give
\[
 K_n\sim\frac{\log n}{\log\log n},
 \qquad r_n=\left(\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^{\gamma},
 \qquad b_{\mu,n}=O(K_n^{-\gamma})=O(r_n).                       \tag{7}
\]
Here all class indices, \(m\), and \(\alpha\) are fixed.  Moreover,
\[
 \log\left(\frac{e_{p,n}}{r_n}\right)
 =-\frac12\log n+O(\log\log n)\longrightarrow-\infty,           \tag{8}
\]
so \(e_{p,n}=o(r_n)\).  Combining (7) and (8) shows that the right-hand side of (6) is \(o(r_n)\).  This proves every assertion, and the constants and probability bounds used above are uniform over \(P\in\mathcal M\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The table now names the precise in-core result informed by each comparator while preserving that none supplies the paper's blind marked qualitative band or the still-open sharp-rate converse.

prose_updates.tldr: This is a statistical-inference paper about a causal ADRF under two blind, independent, nonidentical, asymmetric replicates. The class allows every \(\beta>1/2\) and every fixed error-moment order \(q_e>1\); its moment radius itself yields a common nonvanishing neighborhood, so no separate local spectral-modulus restriction is assumed and open spectral zero sets remain allowed. Analytic cocycle identification and an explicit structural response-surface condition establish the causal identifying functional. Two simultaneous bands are distinguished: an explicit finite relaxed outer-sieve construction is uniformly honest and clipped to \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), while an abstract noncomputational exact-class construction is uniformly honest with uniformly \(o(1)\) expected maximal width. Neither construction proves the candidate \(r_n\) rate. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli lower modulus remains unresolved, so there is no matched honest-band rate.

project_justification.gap: Existing statistical results cover blind repeated-measurement density estimation, confidence bands under auxiliary-error, symmetric-error, or fixed-operator designs, and pointwise continuous-treatment inference. They do not provide a shrinking uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band for blind nonidentical asymmetric replicate errors with open spectral zero sets. The present exact-class compactness argument proves qualitative uniform consistency over \(\beta>1/2\) signals and errors with a fixed \(q_e>1\) moment radius, but supplies no quantitative inverse modulus. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus needed for a sharp all-band converse also remains unproved.
project_justification.niche: The inferential niche is a nonlinear severe inverse problem: compact treatment support supplies entire signal and marked transforms, one centered replicate fixes translation, and the fixed \(q_e>1\) moment bound yields the uniform protected neighborhood \(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\), \(c_*=1/2\) needed for qualitative cocycle inversion. The causal target is a stratum-weighted quotient. A jointly measurable response surface driven by an exogenous random element and continuity of the stratum-specific causal mean bridge that observed regression quotient to the point-dose causal curve. The distinction between qualitative identification and quantitative confidence-set diameter is essential here.
project_justification.fill: The paper delivers two inference maps over the same enlarged class. The explicit map uses deterministic spline, frequency, truncation, and atomic dimensions; simultaneous probability-, marked-, and mass-channel radii; relaxed compact outer signal sieves; a joint feasible set; and measurable clipped ADRF extrema. A Jackson inequality with supremum error of order \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) is recorded for the full range \(\beta>1/2\). This map proves uniform simultaneous coverage and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), but no shrinkage. In parallel, exact empirical-channel residuals are profiled over a compact projected nuisance class. Compactness, expanding-grid equality, the moment-derived protected neighborhood, and marked cocycle injectivity prove that this abstract exact-class band is uniformly honest and has uniformly \(o(1)\) expected maximal width. The qualitative argument supplies no explicit modulus, and the sharp \(O(r_n)\) upper and matching marked converse remain open.

sampling_model.treatment: The observed replicates satisfy \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\). The errors are independent of the latent variables and of one another, need not be identically distributed or symmetric, and may have open spectral zero sets. Location is fixed by \(E[U_2]=0\). For one fixed \(q_e>1\), they obey \(\max_jE|U_j|^{q_e}\le M_e\); consequently \(|\phi_j(t)|\ge1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}\ge1/2\) whenever \(|t|\le(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\), rather than by a separate spectral-modulus assumption.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For any \(\beta>1/2\), the explicit conservative procedure uses relaxed order-\(d\) B-spline families for \(f_x,q_x\), finite atomic characteristic-function families for the two errors, and \(p_x\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) against simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel restrictions on \(\mathcal D_n\); its outer splines are feasibility devices rather than asserted model laws. The error sieves enforce the fixed \(q_e>1\) moment radius and centering, while their common protected neighborhood is derived from that radius. A second, abstract procedure profiles the same empirical radii with no approximation allowances over the exact compact projected class \(\mathscr K\), then takes clipped extrema of \(\mu_{\vartheta}\). The latter is an infinite-dimensional existence construction and is not claimed to be computationally implementable.

prose_updates.related_work: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy provide the unmarked probability-channel cocycle, constrained polynomial estimator, and compact-support \(L^2\) minimax experiment that inform the analytic machinery. Their H1--H2 identification class imposes neither a common error-moment radius nor a uniform local spectral modulus and identifies only up to translation. This paper instead centers the second error and, for uniform inference, fixes a \(q_e>1\) moment radius; the elementary bound \(|\phi_j(t)|\ge1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}\) then derives the uniform protected neighborhood rather than assuming one. Their Theorem 4 is an unmarked \(L^2\)-density converse and does not imply an ADRF-band converse. Their rate proof also uses a protected-region integrated contrast with nearly parametric forward error and does not supply a Lipschitz inverse for the present grid set whose tolerance contains polynomial Jackson error. Gassiat, Le Corff, and Lehéricy supply the broader analytic-continuation principle for blind deconvolution. Huang and Zhang formulate the error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF and derive pointwise inference with a known everywhere-nonzero error transform. Kato and Sasaki develop deconvolution bands under auxiliary-error or conventional spectral designs, which differ from two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates and do not include the marked quotient with joint cell-mass profiling. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura invert Kotlarski restrictions to retain coverage without completeness, but do not establish a shrinking marked-quotient band here. Babii studies honest expected diameter for fixed linear inverse operators. Low supplies a testing-to-expected-length reduction only after a marked modulus is established. None of these sources proves the missing quantitative diameter or fixed-nuisance marked lower modulus for this problem.
prose_updates.interpretation: The observed two-channel law identifies the continuous regression curve \(q_x/f_x\). The nonvanishing neighborhood required to initiate the cocycle is guaranteed uniformly by the \(q_e>1\) moment radius; analytic continuation then accommodates zeros away from that neighborhood. Structural exogeneity equates the observed regression curve with the stratum-specific causal mean almost everywhere in dose, and positivity plus continuity extends the equality to every target dose. Coordinatewise weak unconfoundedness and almost-sure consistency alone would not suffice because they permit treatment-dependent diagonal modifications on null sets.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The causal bridge, analytic-cocycle identification, simultaneous transform concentration, Jackson and relaxed outer-sieve embedding for every \(\beta>1/2\), and clipped uniform coverage are proved. A fixed \(q_e>1\) error-moment radius is sufficient both for first-moment uniform integrability and for a derived protected spectral neighborhood; no separate local-modulus assumption remains. The finite grid-sieve set has no quantitative inverse modulus and therefore no shrinking-width guarantee. Exact-class compactness yields a separate uniformly honest band with uniformly \(o(1)\) expected width, but gives no rate, tuning law, or finite algorithm. The sharp-rate program still requires a protected-cube analytic-polynomial confidence construction for both probability and signed marked channels. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli outcome modulus remains the lower-side obstruction.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The model fixes compact dose support, bounded outcomes, Sobolev radii with \(\beta>1/2\), overlap, finite-stratum masses, the structural causal response surface, and an error \(q_e\)-moment radius for some fixed \(q_e>1\). It does not assume a local spectral modulus: \(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\) and \(c_*=1/2\) follow uniformly from the moment bound, while spectral zeros outside that neighborhood are allowed. The explicit finite relaxed outer-sieve band is uniformly honest for all sufficiently large \(n\) and universally clipped to width at most \(2B_Y\), with no proved shrinkage. The parallel exact-class band is abstract and noncomputational; it is uniformly honest and its expected maximal width is uniformly \(o(1)\), but no explicit rate follows. In particular, no \(O(r_n)\), minimax-matching, or rate-elbow claim is made. The matching-converse kernel remains open as \(\mathrm{oeq{:}fixed\text{-}nuisance\text{-}marked\text{-}modulus}\).

statement_notes.consumer: The bound adds cell-count uncertainty to coverage and proves that mass uncertainty is \(o(r_n)\) throughout the enlarged range \(\beta>1/2\), because only \(\gamma=\beta-1/2>0\) is used; it does not assert a shrinking total band diameter.
